entries.1:1: This book begins by saying that the message inside really came from God and was given to a man named Joel. It reminds the reader that what follows is not just human opinion but a word from God.
entries.1:2: Joel calls on the older leaders and everyone living in the land to pay attention to something terrible that has happened. He asks whether anything like it has ever occurred before in their lifetime or their ancestors' lifetime.
entries.1:3: The people are told to pass the story of this disaster down to their children and grandchildren. It matters that each generation remembers what God has done and what has happened to His people.
entries.1:4: A series of locust swarms came one after another, and each wave ate whatever the previous one had left behind. The point is that the destruction was total, leaving nothing for the people.
entries.1:5: Those who were used to drinking and partying are told to wake up and weep, because the wine they loved is gone. It means that comfort and pleasure can be stripped away suddenly, so don't build your life on them.
entries.1:6: A vast, countless army has invaded the land, and its bite is as fierce as a lion's. This pictures an overwhelming enemy or plague that the people cannot resist.
entries.1:7: The invader has destroyed the grapevines and fig trees, knocking the fruit to the ground and leaving the branches bare and white. It shows how completely the land's food supply has been ruined.
entries.1:8: The people are told to mourn like a young widow grieving the husband she lost early. It means their loss is real and deep, and it is right to grieve over it.
entries.1:9: The offerings that were supposed to be brought to God's house have stopped because there is nothing left to offer. The priests who serve God are grieving, showing that the disaster has touched worship itself.
entries.1:10: The fields are ruined and the land is dry, with no grain, no new wine, and no olive oil. It means the basic things people depend on for food and daily life have all failed.
entries.1:11: The farmers and vineyard workers are ashamed and cry out because their crops of wheat and barley are destroyed. It means hard work has come to nothing, and those who grow food are hurting.
entries.1:12: The vines, fig trees, pomegranates, palms, and apple trees have all dried up, and joy has disappeared from people's lives. It shows that when the land suffers, human happiness suffers too.
entries.1:13: The priests are told to put on rough mourning clothes and spend the night in sorrow because the offerings to God have stopped. It means even the religious leaders must take the disaster seriously and humble themselves.
entries.1:14: The people are called to gather for a special time of fasting and prayer at God's house, including the elders and everyone in the land. It means the right response to crisis is to come together and cry out to God.
entries.1:15: Joel warns that the day of the Lord is near, a day of destruction from the Almighty. It means God is not distant from what is happening; judgment is real and close at hand.
entries.1:16: The people can see with their own eyes that food has been cut off and that joy and gladness have vanished from God's house. It means the loss is visible and undeniable, affecting both daily life and worship.
entries.1:17: The seed has shriveled under the ground, and the storehouses and granaries are empty and broken down because there is no harvest. It means the food supply has failed all the way from planting to storage.
entries.1:18: The animals groan in pain because there is no grass, and the cattle and sheep are confused and scattered. It shows that the disaster hurts not only people but also the creatures that depend on the land.
entries.1:19: Joel cries out to the Lord because fire has burned up the pastures and every tree in the fields. It means he turns to God in prayer as the only hope when everything around is destroyed.
entries.1:20: Even the wild animals look to God for help because the streams have dried up and the pastures are burned. It means all creation depends on God, and people should turn to Him too when things are desperate.
entries.2:1: A warning signal is being raised because God's judgment day is coming. It means we should take God's warnings seriously and not ignore them.
entries.2:2: A dark, frightening day is near, brought by a huge invading army unlike anything seen before. It means judgment is real and should not be dismissed as empty threat.
entries.2:3: The invading army destroys everything in its path, turning a lush land into a wasteland. It means nothing can escape the damage when God allows judgment to come.
entries.2:4: The attackers move like charging horses. It means the danger is fast, powerful, and hard to stop.
entries.2:5: The army sounds like roaring fire and rumbling chariots as it advances. It means the threat is loud, overwhelming, and organized for battle.
entries.2:6: People are overcome with pain and fear when the army arrives. It means real terror comes to those caught in judgment.
entries.2:7: The soldiers march in perfect order and climb walls without breaking ranks. It means the attack is disciplined and cannot easily be resisted.
entries.2:8: They push forward without breaking formation, even through defenses. It means nothing can slow or scatter this advancing force.
entries.2:9: They storm the city, climb walls, and enter houses like thieves. It means no place feels safe from the invasion.
entries.2:10: The earth and sky react with shaking and darkness as the army comes. It means even creation itself is disturbed by God's judgment.
entries.2:11: The Lord leads this mighty army and His voice thunders ahead of it. It means the judgment is God's own doing, and no one can stand against Him.
entries.2:12: Even now God invites His people to return to Him sincerely, with fasting and tears. It means it is not too late to turn back to God.
entries.2:13: God wants changed hearts, not just outward rituals, because He is merciful and slow to anger. It means genuine repentance matters more than religious show.
entries.2:14: Perhaps God will relent and leave a blessing behind instead of destruction. It means there is hope that God may show mercy.
entries.2:15: A signal is given to call a fast and a sacred gathering. It means the whole community should respond to God together.
entries.2:16: Everyone is called to gather, from elders to babies to newlyweds. It means no one is exempt from seeking God in a crisis.
entries.2:17: The priests are to weep and plead with God not to let His people be shamed before the nations. It means leaders should pray earnestly for God's mercy and reputation.
entries.2:18: The Lord responded with concern for His land and compassion for His people. It means God cares and acts when His people turn to Him.
entries.2:19: God promises to restore grain, wine, and oil and to stop His people's shame. It means God's mercy brings real provision and dignity back.
entries.2:20: God promises to drive the northern invader far away and destroy it. It means God Himself removes the threat from His people.
entries.2:21: The land is told not to fear but to rejoice because God has done great things. It means God's restoration gives reason for joy instead of fear.
entries.2:22: Even the animals need not fear, because pastures, trees, and vines are producing again. It means God's blessing reaches all of creation.
entries.2:23: God's people are called to rejoice because He gives rain in due season and restores crops. It means God faithfully provides for those who trust Him.
entries.2:24: The threshing floors and vats will overflow with grain, wine, and oil. It means God's restoration is abundant, not stingy.
entries.2:25: God promises to repay the years that locusts and other pests devoured. It means God can restore what was lost during hard times.
entries.2:26: With full stomachs, the people will praise the Lord who has done wonders for them. It means God's blessings should lead us to thank and praise Him.
entries.2:27: God's people will know He is among them and that He alone is their God, and they will never be shamed. It means God's presence and faithfulness give lasting security.
entries.2:28: God promises to pour out His Spirit on all kinds of people, and sons, daughters, old men, and young men will receive dreams and visions. It means God's Spirit is available broadly, not just to a select few.
entries.2:29: Even servants and servant girls will receive God's Spirit. It means God's gift is not limited by social status or gender.
entries.2:30: God will show signs in the sky and on earth, like blood, fire, and smoke. It means God is at work in dramatic, visible ways before the end.
entries.2:31: The sun will darken and the moon turn red before the great and fearful day of the Lord. It means cosmic signs will announce that God's judgment is near.
entries.2:32: Everyone who calls on the Lord's name will be saved, and a remnant will be preserved in Zion and Jerusalem. It means salvation is available to anyone who turns to God, and He keeps a faithful remnant.
entries.3:1: God promises that a time is coming when he will reverse the bad situation of his people and restore their fortunes. For the reader, it means hardship is not the end of the story when God steps in.
entries.3:2: God will gather the nations who harmed his people and hold them accountable for scattering Israel and dividing up their land. It means God sees injustice done to his people and will call the guilty to answer for it.
entries.3:3: The nations treated human lives as cheap, trading a boy for a prostitute and a girl for a drink. It means God notices when people are treated as things to be bought and sold, and he does not ignore it.
entries.3:4: God challenges Tyre, Sidon, and Philistia, asking whether they are trying to pay him back for something, and warns that any repayment will quickly fall back on them. It means God is not in debt to anyone and will turn their hostility back on themselves.
entries.3:5: These nations took Israel's silver, gold, and treasured items and put them in their temples to their gods. It means God takes seriously when what belongs to him and his people is carried off and used for false worship.
entries.3:6: They sold the people of Judah and Jerusalem to the Greeks, sending them far from home. It means God remembers when people are uprooted and sold away from their land.
entries.3:7: God says he will bring his people back from the places they were sold to and turn the harm done to them back on the heads of those who did it. It means God promises rescue for the oppressed and consequences for the oppressors.
entries.3:8: God will let Judah sell the sons and daughters of these nations to a distant people, Sheba, as payment. It means the same measure of justice will be applied to those who enslaved others, and God declares it will happen.
entries.3:9: God calls the nations to prepare for war and wake up their fighting men. It means a day of reckoning is being announced, and no one can stay neutral or asleep.
entries.3:10: People are told to turn farming tools into weapons and for the weak to say they are strong. It means the coming conflict will be total, and even the feeble are drawn into it.
entries.3:11: The nations are urged to gather quickly, and God is asked to bring his own mighty ones down too. It means the scene is set for a decisive showdown, with God himself involved.
entries.3:12: The nations are summoned to the valley of Jehoshaphat, where God will sit as judge over them all. It means God himself will preside over the judgment of the nations.
entries.3:13: The harvest is ripe and the winepress is full and overflowing because the nations' evil is so great. It means judgment is ready to fall, pictured as a harvest and winepress because of their wrongdoing.
entries.3:14: Crowds upon crowds fill the valley of decision, because the day of the Lord is near. It means a great and decisive day of God's judgment is coming soon.
entries.3:15: The sun, moon, and stars go dark and stop shining. It means the day of the Lord brings cosmic signs that something huge and unsettling is happening.
entries.3:16: The Lord thunders from Zion and shakes the heavens and earth, but he is a shield and strong refuge for his people. It means God's power is terrifying to his enemies but protective for those who belong to him.
entries.3:17: God's people will know he is the Lord dwelling in Zion, and Jerusalem will be holy with no outsiders passing through. It means God's presence will be unmistakable and his city set apart for him.
entries.3:18: In that day the mountains will drip sweet wine, the hills flow with milk, streams fill with water, and a fountain flows from the Lord's house to water the valley. It means God's blessing will be abundant and life-giving everywhere.
entries.3:19: Egypt and Edom will become desolate because of the evil and bloodshed they committed against Judah. It means nations that shed innocent blood will face ruin, not escape.
entries.3:20: Judah and Jerusalem will be inhabited forever, from generation to generation. It means God's people will have a lasting home and will not be wiped out.
entries.3:21: God will punish the bloodshed that had gone unpunished, because he lives in Zion. It means no injustice stays forgotten forever, and God himself guarantees justice from his dwelling place.
